prompt: Run a group of statements as one transaction: commit when they all succeed, roll back when any of them throws. Complete runAll in TransactionLog, then run the tests.
explanation: A transaction is all-or-nothing: begin marks the start, commit makes every change permanent at once, and rollback throws the whole group away. The try block covers all the executes plus the commit, so the catch can undo a partial transaction no matter which statement failed. Returning true or false lets the caller see the outcome without having to handle the exception itself -- and because the loop stops at the first failure, later statements never run.
hints: Call begin() before the try block -- there is nothing to roll back until the transaction has started.
Put the loop over statements AND the commit() inside the same try block.
catch (RuntimeException e) is enough here; inside the catch call rollback() and return false.
